chunks: And with Thamud who carved rocks in the valley;
ai.seo_question: Who were the Thamud and what did they carve in the valley?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the architectural prowess of Thamud, who carved homes into the mountains of Al-Hijr, as a sign of their arrogance and self-sufficiency before divine retribution. The reference to 'the valley' (Al-Wadi) specifically identifies the region of Al-Hijr, linking their physical grandeur with their spiritual downfall. This serves as a timeless lesson on how material strength, when divorced from divine humility, leads to destruction.
